name: vibe-ops
description: Workspace root. The Claude Code plugin lives in plugin/ and has no build; the CLI's packages live in cli/packages/.

scripts._comment_build: core first, explicitly. `--workspaces` runs in directory order, not dependency order, so `cli` sorts before `core`, `records` and `module-harness` and would typecheck against their stale dist and report success. A package earns a place here by being STATICALLY imported by something that sorts ahead of it; module-harness qualifies because cli/src/harness-status.ts imports it by name, unlike every other module-*, which cli only ever reaches through a dynamic import().
scripts.build:foundation: npm run build -w @entelekheia/vibe-ops-core && npm run build -w @entelekheia/governance-base && npm run build -w @entelekheia/governance-plan && npm run build -w @entelekheia/vibe-ops-harness
scripts.build: npm run build:foundation && npm run build --workspaces --if-present
scripts._comment_clean: `tsc` only ever writes; it never removes. So a renamed or deleted source leaves its old artifact in dist/ and every consumer keeps resolving it — and because most tests import ../src directly while a module loaded through its package `exports` resolves to dist/, a run can exercise the new source and the stale build at once and pass. Not folded into `build`, which stays incremental for the edit loop; folded into `pretest`, where a wrong green is the expensive outcome.
scripts.pretest: npm run clean && npm run build

_comment_overrides: tree-sitter-markdown@0.3.2 declares a peer of tree-sitter ^0.21.1 and tree-sitter-yaml@0.7.1 declares ^0.22.4; the pin is 0.25.1, measured (2026-08-10, project/tasks/001-the-document-model-and-its-sensor.md for markdown, project/tasks/002-the-injection-resolver.md for yaml) to produce a byte-for-byte identical parse tree across 0.21.1/0.22.4/0.25.1 on darwin-arm64. Both peer ranges are conservative, not load-bearing.
